questions.question: A trailer will swing around most when:
questions.correctAnswerText: It is empty.
questions.explanation: An empty trailer swings out and strikes other vehicles more easily than a loaded one. It also needs a longer stopping distance.

questions.question: If you drive a vehicle built before 1998 and are not sure if the trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you can:

options.text: Check for wheel speed sensors on the back of the brakes.
Look for a red light on the front right corner of the converter dolly.
Pump the air brakes to turn on the ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for wheel speed sensors on the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes. This will tell you if ABS is present.

questions.question: If your trailer goes off course while backing, you should:

options.text: Pull forward, readjust, and back up again.
Get out and move the trailer by hand.
Turn the steering wheel all the way left until the trailer straightens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward, readjust, and back up again.
questions.explanation: Pull your truck forward to reposition your vehicle. Then back up again.

questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: Keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
Prevents the truck from being stolen.
Prevents the driver from going too fast.
Prevents the trailer from being released by accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.

questions.question: An automatic tractor protection valve will pop out when:

options.text: Air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
Wheels regain traction after a skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: When air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi, the valve pops out and closes to stop air flow.

questions.question: Pull out the trailer air supply control to test:
questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes.
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before each trip. Pull out the trailer air supply control and pull forward slightly with the tractor. The trailer should not move.

questions.question: The ____ air line is controlled by either the foot brake or trailer hand brake.
questions.correctAnswerText: Service
questions.explanation: The service air line is controlled by the foot brake or hand brake. It is also called the control or signal line. This line connects to relay valves, which apply the trailer brakes more quickly.

questions.question: Not keeping the fifth wheel plate properly greased could cause:
questions.correctAnswerText: Steering problems.
questions.explanation: Without proper lubrication, friction builds up between the tractor and trailer. This causes steering problems.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination:

options.text: Cargo weight must be split evenly between all trailers.
The heaviest trailer should be right behind the cab.
The heaviest trailer should be in the rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The heaviest trailer should be right behind the cab.
questions.explanation: The heaviest trailer should be closest to the tractor. The lightest trailer should be in the rear.

questions.question: An air supply control lever should be in its "normal" position when you are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Pulling a trailer.
questions.explanation: In older vehicles, the air supply control may be a lever. When it is in the "normal" position, it is properly set for pulling a trailer.

questions.question: How can you best tell that your trailer is starting to skid?

options.text: By looking at other drivers' faces.
By seeing it in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: By seeing it in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: The best way to recognize a trailer skid early is to see the trailer moving sideways in your mirrors.

questions.question: What is the service air line attached to?
questions.correctAnswerText: Relay valves.
questions.explanation: The service air line is attached to relay valves. These valves let the trailer brakes work quickly when you use the foot brake or trailer hand brake.

questions.question: How do you test the tractor protection valve?

options.text: Remove the parking brake control knob.
Release air using the brake pedal.
Release air using the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air using the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Test the tractor protection valve by letting the air system fill, turning off the engine, and then pressing the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to emergency position when air pressure gets too low.

questions.question: What happens when you push in the trailer air supply control?

options.text: It turns off the air brakes.
It sends air to the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It sends air to the trailer.
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull it out to stop the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: What can happen when you simply change lanes?

options.text: A whip-like effect that can cause the truck to roll over.
Other drivers get confused about which lane you want.

questions.correctAnswerText: A whip-like effect that can cause the truck to roll over.
questions.explanation: Changing lanes too quickly in a truck can create a whip-like effect that may cause the truck to roll over.

questions.question: ____ cause more than half of all truck driver deaths from accidents.
questions.correctAnswerText: Truck rollovers
questions.explanation: Truck rollovers cause more than half of all accident-related truck driver deaths. To prevent rollovers, load cargo low and centered. Also, take corners slowly.

questions.question: How can you avoid making sudden lane changes?

options.text: Use your horn to tell other drivers to move.
Drive slower than the speed limit.
Watch the road ahead while driving.
Pull over and wait when traffic is heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the road ahead while driving.
questions.explanation: Watch ahead on the road for obstacles. This way you can plan lane changes early and avoid sudden moves.

questions.question: After coupling, how much space should there be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?
questions.correctAnswerText: No space
questions.explanation: After coupling, inspect all connections. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: What does a shut-off valve do?

options.text: It is located on the front of a trailer.
It is located on the instrument panel.
It stops air from leaking out of the brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops air from leaking out of the brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve should always be closed to keep air in the brake system.

questions.question: What should you do after finishing a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Leave the rear shut-off valves open.
Leave the emergency line valve open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the emergency line valve.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, open the rear shut-off valves to check for air leaks. Before you drive, close both shut-off valves.
